sections.overview: The Fieldfare breeds across northern Eurasia and many populations migrate southwest for winter.
sections.identification: Its grey head and rump, chestnut back, black tail and spotted pale breast make it distinctive among thrushes.
sections.habitat: It breeds in open woodland and wooded edges, then uses fields, pasture, orchards and hedges while migrating or wintering.
sections.diet: It eats invertebrates in the breeding season and relies more on berries and fallen fruit in winter.
sections.behavior: In winter it often travels and feeds in noisy flocks; a harsh repeated “chak” call can reveal it.
sections.reproduction: It commonly nests in loose colonies, building a tree nest in which the female lays about five or six eggs.
sections.ecology: In Central Asia, winter flocks may include Black-throated Thrushes (T. atrogularis); see that profile for the shared flocking record. The Ring Ouzel is another Turdus, but a UK summer breeder; see its profile for the contrast.
sections.conservation: In Britain it is a regular winter visitor and is on the RSPB’s UK Red List of Birds of Conservation Concern.
